stem:
A 10-year-old girl with known asthma is brought to the emergency department. She can say only a few words at a time, is using her neck muscles to breathe and has oxygen saturation of 89% in room air. She is alert. She is given oxygen, back-to-back salbutamol via spacer and oral prednisolone. Twenty minutes later she is still working hard to breathe.

Which treatment should be added next, within this first hour?

options.label: A
options.explanation: IV magnesium is the next step if she fails to respond to salbutamol plus ipratropium. It is not given before the first-hour inhaled add-on.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Aminophylline is reserved for critical asthma not responding to other treatment, in an intensive care setting. Its toxicity outweighs benefit at this stage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: In severe acute asthma, ipratropium, an inhaled muscarinic antagonist, is added to salbutamol during the first hour. It reduces vagally mediated bronchoconstriction and adds to the beta-agonist effect.

options.label: D
options.explanation: High-dose inhaled corticosteroid adds nothing to systemic steroid in acute asthma, and she has already had prednisolone.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Montelukast has no role in the treatment of acute severe asthma.

context: In severe acute asthma, give oxygen, frequent salbutamol, a systemic steroid and inhaled ipratropium (a muscarinic antagonist) during the first hour; IV magnesium comes next if she does not respond.
